title: Session Snapshot Onramp: Lightweight Resume & Tool Handoff Proposal (WIP)
content:
Purpose
------
Quick exploration of an opinionated, tiny-surface API for session snapshots + onramp (resume) that plays nicely with streaming responses, tool invocation handoffs, and typed/structured output. Goal: give SDKs a cheap resume token + compact snapshot format that makes resumable UX reliable across flaky mobile/edge networks and enables speculative local tool adaptors. 

Context / problem statements
---------------------------
- Hosted streaming sessions today are single-stream, best-effort. If a client drops, rehydrating state for continuation is painful for clients and servers; we replay a lot or require server-side full conversation history.
- Tool calls (external actions) can be long-running; callers need a way to checkpoint progress and resume without double-executing side effects.
- Mobile/embedded SDKs need a tiny memory/CPU footprint and a simple resume primitive they can reason about.
- We want minimal server-side ceremony to support resume for hosted API while preserving security and auditability.

Design principles
-----------------
- Compact: snapshot should be byte-small (ideally <8KB for typical short sessions) and safe to store in local device storage.
- Idempotent handoff: when resuming a session with pending tool requests, we prefer a two-phase resume handshake to avoid duplicate effect executions.
- Typed/structured first: snapshots carry a small typed index of current tool handles, partial structured outputs, and token cursors rather than raw model state.
- Backwards-compatible: existing streaming endpoints continue to function; resume is opt-in via header or param.
- Observable: resume events and snapshot sizes emitted to telemetry.

Key concepts and primitives
---------------------------
- resume_token: short opaque string (JWT-like, signed by control plane) that references a server-side minimal checkpoint. Contains expiry and scope.
- snapshot_blob: compact, optionally client-storable CBOR/JSON string containing: session_id, model_cursor (token index + rng state fingerprint), outstanding_tool_handles (ids + idempotency keys), partial_structured_output (compact JSON schema fragments), client_mutations_log (small).
- tool_handle: server-side id for a pending tool call + idempotency_key; snapshot includes handle metadata but not tool result bytes unless completed.
- resume_mode: quick-choice param: optimistic (resume local speculative outputs first), canonical-first (validate server state before emitting), safe-two-phase (server confirms pending tool replay allowed).

Example flow sketches
---------------------
1) Normal stream + snapshot generation
   - Client connects streaming endpoint with header X-Resume: enabled.
   - Server periodically emits small in-stream checkpoint events with a base64(snapshot_blob) and resume_token. SDK stores latest pair locally.

   In-stream checkpoint example (server->client event text):
     EVENT: resume-checkpoint
     payload: {"token":"rt_abc123","snapshot":"eyJzI..."}

2) Client drop and resume (safe-two-phase)
   - Client reconnects: POST /v1/resume-session?mode=safe-two-phase Authorization: Bearer <api-key> Resume-Token: rt_abc123
   - Server validates token, re-hydrates minimal checkpoint, compares outstanding tool handles.
   - Server replies: 202 Accepted {"resume_id":"r_456","pending_tools":[{"handle":"t_9","status":"pending"}],"instructions":"replay-tools=false"}
   - Client can choose to locally continue showing speculative text from snapshot while waiting for server confirmation (UI hammer time).

3) Handing tool results without double-exec
   - When server sees a pending tool with idempotency_key present in snapshot, it first checks execution log. If uncompleted, server may re-queue the tool but mark event as "replayed-from-resume" for auditing. If completed, server returns cached result.

SDK ergonomics: minimal API surface
----------------------------------
- SDK exposes three calls: startStream(opts), onCheckpoint(callback(snapshot_blob, token)), resumeSession({token, mode}).
- Checkpoint callback must be lightweight: SDKs recommended to write to secure local store asynchronously.
- Provide a tiny helper to materialize partial structured outputs from snapshot and merge with incoming streaming events.
- Default resume_mode for mobile = optimistic; server-side config can force safe-two-phase for enterprise tenants.

Structured output considerations
-------------------------------
- Snapshots intentionally contain compact structured fragments (e.g., partial JSON schema nodes) to allow clients to render meaningful UI while resuming. We recommend trimming heavy attachment data (images/blobs) and instead include pointers to artifact ids.
- For tool-handshake typed outputs we propose a minimal versioned contract: 
   {"schema_v":1,"tools":[{"id":"t_9","contract":"/schemas/retrieve-ticket-v1","status":"pending"}],"partial_out":"{\"title\":\"Draft reply\"}"}
- Versioning: snapshot_blob must include schema_v and be tolerant to unknown keys. SDKs ignore unknown fields but log them to telemetry.

Telemetry & SLOs
----------------
- Emit metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, avg_snapshot_size, avg_number_of_tool_handles_per_snapshot.
- SLO target: 95% resume_success within 3s for warm sessions (server still in memory), 85% within 5s for cold sessions.
- Track double-execution incidents (should be near-zero); if >0.1% of resumes, trigger incident.

Security & privacy notes
------------------------
- resume_token must be short-lived (default TTL 1 hour) and scoping-limited to session id + tenant id.
- snapshot_blob should avoid containing PII unless tenant explicitly requests; default is scrub sensitive fields.
- Tool handles referencing external systems must carry least-privilege scopes.

Rollout plan (phases)
---------------------
- Alpha (2 weeks): SDK-only feature flags for internal apps, synthetic tests. No persistence by default, only in-memory.
- Beta (6 weeks): opt-in customers; enable in-stream checkpoints; collect telemetry; enable safe-two-phase for critical toolflows.
- GA (3 months after beta): default enable for new tenants; SDKs provide migration helpers.

Open questions / tradeoffs
-------------------------
- Server-side state vs purely client-side resume: how much minimal state must we persist to make resume cheap? Trade CPU/storage vs resume latency.
- Snapshot format: CBOR is compact but less debuggable than JSON. Recommend CBOR wire with base64 when embedded in text streams.
- Tool replay semantics: do we allow automatic replay or force operator decision for side-effectful calls? Default: automatic only when idempotency_key present otherwise operator requires manual resolve.
- SDK UX: how aggressive should optimistic rendering be? Too optimistic risks showing stale/corrected text.

Next steps / actionable tickets
----------------------------
- Create JIRA: API-RESUME-001 define Resume REST surface and headers (owner: Jordan)
- Create JIRA: SDK-RESUME-002 implement checkpoint callback for all language SDKs (owner: Priya)
- Spike: infra cost model for server checkpoint persistence (owner: Luis)
- Security review request: SUBMIT to compliance @security (owner: Maya)

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This is intentionally lightweight and opinionated. Looking for feedback on: snapshot size target, default resume_mode, and tool replay policy.
- Also want SDK lead buy-in on the tiny-surface approach; if we expose too many flags we defeat the ergonomics goal.

Appendix: quick proto examples
-----------------------------
- resume token example: rt_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9... (opaque to SDK)
- compact snapshot (humanized): {session_id: s_123, cursor: 352, handles: [{id:t_9, key:kp_8, name:retrieve-ticket}], partial_out:{title:\"Draft\"}}

-- end of doc --
